key_insight: The paper reports stronger knot ropelength lower bounds: L ≥ 2.0996C^(3/4) in crossing number C and L ≥ π(s−1) in stick number s.
engineering_relevance: These bounds provide geometric benchmarks for thickness-constrained knotted curves, potentially informing computational shape optimization.
method: Use LLM assistance to refine mathematical bounds.
Separate local and global terms in an optimization integral.
Relate ropelength to stick number and optimize a standard torus-knot parameterization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an increase in the universal lower-bound coefficient from 1.105 to 2.0996 and stronger lower bounds for at least 41 torus knots and a class of pretzel knots.
watch_item: The LLM did not help improve known universal upper-bound coefficients or scalings; the abstract alone does not establish proof validity.
paper_title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
